concept: Condorcet winner and the majority principle
definition_and_role: An option that beats every other option in pairwise majority. The majoritarian reading of a compromise, and the second step of QVC.
Majority preferences can be cyclic (Condorcet paradox); how often a Condorcet winner exists depends on the structure of preferences.
The smallest set of options that each beat every option outside it; Condorcet methods differ in how they choose within it.
Condorcet method based on the strongest paths of pairwise victories: Smith-consistent, clone-independent, monotonic, O(m^3). The majority step of QVC.
Locks pairwise majorities from the strongest down unless they close a cycle; clone-independent. Could replace Schulze in QVC.
Discards the weakest majority in every cycle; clone-independent and immune to spoilers, but often not single-winner. Stable Voting refines it to one winner.
The ranking closest to the voters' pairwise preferences; more generally, rules read as the nearest consensus profile. Kemeny is NP-hard.
Condorcet methods that count pairwise wins (Copeland) or minimise the worst defeat (Minimax); neither is independent of clones.
Plurality, Borda and instant-runoff (IRV): score ranks or eliminate by first choices. Vote splitting (plurality), teaming (Borda), non-monotonicity (IRV).

concept: Evaluative rules: approval and Majority Judgment
definition_and_role: Voters approve or grade options; approval elects the most acceptable option, Majority Judgment the best median grade. The acceptability line of the QVC ballot borrows from them.
Maximal lotteries and tournament solutions: lotteries over options unbeaten in expected pairwise majority.

concept: Independence of clones and agenda flooding
definition_and_role: Adding variants of an option must not change the outcome. Required by an open agenda (H1); fails for Borda, fallback bargaining and the proportional veto core.
Arrow: no ranking rule meets Pareto, independence of irrelevant alternatives and non-dictatorship. Gibbard-Satterthwaite: every non-dictatorial rule with 3+ options is manipulable.
How often, by whom and how hard strategic voting is; computational hardness as a barrier; measured by coalitional manipulability.
Condorcet-consistent rules can reward abstention with 4+ options; related: positive and negative involvement.

concept: Single-peaked preferences and the median voter
definition_and_role: With single-peaked preferences the median voter's favourite is the Condorcet winner, and majority rule is transitive.

concept: Spatial voting, chaos and agenda control
definition_and_role: In two or more dimensions majority equilibria rarely exist and cycles span the space, so whoever controls the agenda can steer the outcome.
When quota rules have undominated options: Nakamura number, Greenberg's d/(d+1), the 64% rule. Vetoes make cores non-empty but favour the status quo.
The quota trades decision costs against external costs (Buchanan-Tullock); simple majority maximises expected agreement (Rae).
Comparisons of unanimity with majority rule plus a separate veto: information aggregation, delay, bargaining costs.

concept: Veto players, status-quo bias and gridlock
definition_and_role: More veto players mean more policy stability; with the status quo as default, vetoes become a vote for inertia. Prop. 2: unanimity deadlocks a large assembly.
Proposers and agenda setters gain power from the reversion point, the order of votes and the right to propose.

concept: Dynamic bargaining and endogenous status quo
definition_and_role: When today's decision is tomorrow's status quo: inertia, inefficiency, capture by vetoers.

concept: Number of rounds and fast proposal procedures
definition_and_role: One or two rounds suffice in structured proposal models; more rounds can empower vetoers. QVC uses one ballot and at most one revision round.
Members strike options in turn until one is left; decisive, but not anonymous and not clone-independent.

concept: Proportional veto and the veto core
definition_and_role: Coalitions veto a share of options equal to their share of voters; the core is never empty and computable by max-flow, but fails independence of clones.
The share of voters that guarantees a majority its favourites against the share that lets a minority exclude its worst options.

concept: Compromise by descent: fallback bargaining and majoritarian compromise
definition_and_role: Voters descend their rankings in lockstep until all (fallback bargaining) or a majority (majoritarian compromise) agree.
Shortlisting, alternating vetoes and veto-rank between two parties; strategic properties and the meaning of a compromise.
Rough consensus (objections addressed, not unanimity) and tacit consent: how organisations decide without formal individual vetoes.
Blocking minorities, default options, quorums and supermajorities in real institutions; the liberum veto as the failure case.

concept: Evaluating rules with simulations and data
definition_and_role: Comparing rules on random cultures and real ballots: Condorcet efficiency, utility efficiency, probability models, preference libraries.

concept: Communication, accountability and experiments in committees
definition_and_role: Laboratory and theoretical work on how deliberation, communication and responsibility for one's vote change committee outcomes.
A limited stock of votes or vetoes across decisions, spent where members care most; a safeguard against routine blocking.
Under incomplete information, the best use of a veto player can be to let them choose within an interval fixed in advance.
